groups.title: Database
groups.intro: Semaphore creates and migrates its own tables on start. Pick the dialect before the first run; changing it later means migrating the data yourself.

groups.title: Web server
groups.intro: Where the HTTP server listens and how users reach it. Set `web_host` to the URL users type: redirect URIs, webhook targets, and links in notifications are built from it.

groups.title: Paths and storage
groups.intro: Directories used for repositories, task workspaces, secret files and SSH sockets. Secret directories may contain persistent credentials; do not treat every directory as disposable cache.

groups.title: Encryption
groups.intro: Keys that protect stored secrets. Back them up separately from the database: the database is unreadable without them.

groups.title: Authentication
groups.intro: How users sign in. See [Authentication](/admin-guide/authentication) for the provider-side setup.

groups.title: Global credential providers
groups.intro: Vault/OpenBao connection metadata. Bootstrap credentials are supplied separately through provider-specific environment variables; see [Additional schemas](configuration-schemas.md#native-process-variables).

groups.title: Tasks
groups.intro: Concurrency, retention, and the environment task processes run in.

groups.title: Runners
groups.intro: Server-side switches first, then the keys a runner reads from its own configuration file. See [Runners](/admin-guide/runners).

groups.title: Task JWT
groups.intro: Short-lived tokens that identify a task to external systems. See [Task JWTs](/user-guide/task-templates/jwt).

groups.title: Logging and metrics
groups.intro: Where server, event, and task logs go, and the Prometheus endpoint. See [Logs](/admin-guide/logs) and [Metrics](/admin-guide/metrics).

groups.title: Teams and invitations
groups.intro: How people are added to projects. See [Teams](/user-guide/team).

groups.title: High availability
groups.intro: Running several nodes against one database. See [High availability](/admin-guide/ha).

groups.title: Debugging
groups.intro: Switches useful when diagnosing a problem. Do not leave them on in production.
